I feel like this needs some greater context. Besides the prefix what makes it definitely a Vorkosigan/Scalzi reference? Is Brandel a character in the other series? -- ''[[User:Nae'blis|nae]]'[[User_talk:Nae'blis|blis]]'' 18:45, 25 June 2024 (UTC)
: Lois Mcmaster Bujold, not Scalzi. It ''could'' be coincidence, but Vordarian is spelled exactly the same in both and it doesn't seem to exist as a name anywhere else other than Towers of Midnight and Barrayar (1991). Barrayar won the Hugo Award for best novel and is the first novel where we see the protagonist. Three other novels in the series also won the Hugo Award for best novel and five more were nominated. The Vordarian in the book isn't important outside of that one novel, but has a historical importance and casts a permanent shadow over the life of the protagonist. Vorkosigan might have been too on the nose to pick as inspiration. Given the profile of the series, it would be hard to imagine Sanderson not being aware of it. Yeah, I would normally take name inspirations with a pinch of salt, but it is spelled *exactly* the same and doesn't really fit the Andoran flavor.
